description: HELMpy provides Holomorphic Embedding Load-flow and Newton-Raphson power-flow solvers in Python. Tulio Molina and Juan Jose Ortega developed it at Universidad de los Andes in Venezuela for research on electrical network solution methods. The repository contains core solver modules, sample grids, computed reference results and MATLAB helpers for converting MATPOWER cases to spreadsheets. Users choose the network, buses and slack-bus representation; spatial coverage is therefore any configured electrical grid, and outputs describe a steady state, not a time-domain transient. Code is free under AGPL-3.0-or-later. It can support power-flow comparisons and capacity-analysis workflows. Related model-pandapower documents HELMpy as a separately installed alternative solver. A limitation is the README compatibility statement for Python 3.6 and 3.7, so current environments need checking. The sample grids and user guide were identified without downloading their payloads. No solver was installed and no reference result was reproduced.
